message: Writing the guide from what the agent found
Re-checking 8 key claims against their sources

text: I should fetch these URLs in parallel to save time.

I'm going through each claim one by one: c20 looks supported by the Advanced Access, App Review, and Business Verification text. For c23, I'm checking whether the screencast requirement, working reviewer credentials, public privacy policy, and consistent domains are all backed up by the cited sources.

On consistent domains specifically, I'm noticing it's only explicitly covered in one source but not the other cited page, so I'll mark it as partial rather than fully supported.

Then c5 checks out — the overview text confirms users need a professional (business or creator) account to use the APIs. For c27, I'm verifying common rejection reasons: unreproducible screencasts, test credentials failing during review, app changes mid-review, incomplete Business Verification, and policy violations, cross-referencing each against the sources that mention them.

For c1, the Composio page is too generic — it doesn't actually reference Instagram or the specific managed OAuth slug, so that claim isn't substantiated. For c11, the page frames the scope deprecation in future tense ("will be deprecated") rather than confirming it already happened, so I'm treating the claim as partially supported since it asserts past-tense failure that the page doesn't quite state directly. Finally, c16 and c18 both check out cleanly against their respective pages regarding Standard Access requirements and Advanced Access limitations.

evidence: The cited Composio page describes managed OAuth apps generally and says Composio maintains the OAuth registration for toolkits with managed OAuth. It does not mention Instagram, a slug 'instagram', or a managed=true flag, and it tells readers to check per toolkit via the API.

The overview says the Instagram Platform serves Instagram professional accounts, including businesses and creators, and that "To use the APIs, your app users must have an Instagram professional account."

The Instagram API with Instagram Login page says the old scope values "will be deprecated on January 27, 2025" and that failure to update "will result in your app being unable to call the Instagram endpoints." The page is written in future tense, so it does not itself confirm the deprecation took effect.
The Business Login page states: "Standard Access if your app serves Instagram professional accounts you own or manage and have added to your app in the App Dashboard."
The overview says: "some features might not work properly until your app has been granted Advanced Access. This might limit the functionality of any test apps you use."

The overview says Advanced Access is required if the app serves professional accounts the developer doesn't own or manage, and can be used by app users without a role on the app or claiming business portfolio. It states: "This access level requires App Review and Business Verification."

Both cited blogs support the screencast point (show login, consent screen, and feature end to end; Dojo Labs: "Record it end to end") and reviewer test credentials (Dojo Labs: give "a password that does not expire and no two-factor step"). Dojo Labs also covers a public privacy policy and data deletion URL. Neither cited page explicitly says 'consistent domains'; that appears only on the uncited singhamandeep page, and the Saurabh Dhar page only says to keep permissions, features, screencast and credentials consistent.

Across the cited pages: Saurabh Dhar says the reviewer must reproduce the use case and that a screencast must show the permission in use; singhamandeep lists test credentials stopping during review, the app changing mid-review, and Business Verification not completed; Saurabh Dhar's 'Unable to approve permission request' post says Meta defaults to rejection under Developer Policy 1.9.
